text:
You need a real-time webcam system that can classify whether a watch is genuine and predict its current state from bulk image data.

I’m Noor Halden, and I have 6 years of experience building machine learning and deep learning systems with Python, PyTorch, scikit-learn, and computer vision workflows. I can help you preprocess the watch images, train a robust CNN-based classifier, and prepare it for fast inference in a web app.

In Ceramic tile defect detection, I built a camera-based crack and chip detector exported to ONNX and running on an industrial PC beside the kiln line, reaching 97.4% recall on cracks and reducing false rejects from 8% to 2.1%. In Satellite crop classification, I built a segmentation model that labels field parcels into 6 crop types from Sentinel-2 imagery, reaching a mean IoU of 0.74 across 6 crop classes.

Would you like the model to return both authenticity and state in one prediction, or as two separate outputs?
